findings.text: `source < existing_source` compares two `ParameterSource` members. In upstream click `ParameterSource` is a plain `enum.Enum`, not an `IntEnum`, and I couldn't check this in the repo. If so, the comparison raises `TypeError` whenever two options share a name and the slot already has a source, which is the feature-switch case this patch targets. If the enum is ordered, the order (COMMANDLINE, ENVIRONMENT, DEFAULT, DEFAULT_MAP, PROMPT) is implicit and was never intended as a precedence ranking.

The old code let the first parameter keep a shared slot. `same_source and not auto_would_downgrade_explicit` now lets a later parameter with the same source overwrite it. Example: `--a/--b` flags that both use the name `mode` and both fall back to DEFAULT. The last-declared option's default now wins even when neither is explicit, or when both are explicit. If `--a --b` are both passed on the command line, the later-processed one now wins instead of the first.

Parameter source is now recorded only for the winning option, and only when no source exists yet. A losing option that reads a different source, such as ENVIRONMENT, has that source dropped when the slot's source is already set and the new source isn't more explicit. A related problem: `existing_value is UNSET` can be true while `existing_source` is already set, because a non-exposed param or a param whose value was UNSET claimed it. The slot then counts as empty and is overwritten without comparing sources, so `ctx.get_parameter_source` can disagree with the value actually stored.

0.reason: The patch does not include the definition of ParameterSource, so whether `source < existing_source` raises TypeError cannot be determined from the code.

1.reason: The new same_source tie-break allows a later parameter with the same source to overwrite an earlier one, changing the documented first-wins behavior for shared slots.
